en.headline: Police receive 130 reports of suspected iPhone Duo credit card misuse, involving HK$5…
en.dek: As of 9am on Monday, the number of people reporting unauthorised charges for online smartphone purchases has risen, with cases handed to the cybercrime unit.
body: Hong Kong police said that as of 9am on Monday they had received reports from 130 people who suspected their credit cards had been misused for online purchases of smartphones, involving about HK$5 million.

The cases, linked to pre-orders of the iPhone Duo that opened on Friday evening, have been classified as obtaining property by deception and referred to the Cyber Security and Technology Crime Bureau. No arrests have been made.

Earlier reports on Saturday put the figure at more than 110 cases involving about HK$4.6 million. Police have previously expressed regret that the company did not activate additional verification measures after a similar incident last month, and investigations continue.

zh.headline: 警接130人報稱信用卡被盜用買iPhone Duo 涉款約500萬元
zh.dek: 警方周一表示截至上午九時，共接獲130宗懷疑信用卡被盜用於網上購買智能電話的報案，涉及金額約500萬元，案件交由網絡安全及科技罪案調查科跟進。
body: 警方今日表示，截至上午九時，共接獲130人報稱懷疑信用卡被盜用於網上購買智能電話，涉及金額約500萬元。案件暫列以欺騙手段取得財產，交由網絡安全及科技罪案調查科調查，暫無人被捕。
事件與周五晚上開放預購的iPhone Duo有關。警方較早前於周六曾表示接獲逾110宗同類報案，涉款約460萬元。
警方早前指對公司未有積極採取預防措施感到遺憾，並繼續調查有否同一犯罪集團涉及。市民如發現可疑交易應立即聯絡銀行及報警。
